result.instructions:
Trading gateway for binary-options (fixed-expiry call/put options: you stake an amount on the price being above or below the open quote at expiration; a winning position pays the stake plus profit_percent of it, a losing one forfeits the stake).

Typical workflow: list_balances (pick a balance_id) → list_assets (pick an asset_id; note its profit_percent, minimum_amount/maximum_amount and available expirations) → get_candles for recent price context → place_trade (direction 'call' or 'put', an expired timestamp picked from the asset's expirations list in list_assets, the amount, and the asset's profit_percent). Use list_positions and get_trade_history to review. sell_position closes an open position early at the current buyback price where the asset allows it (buyback_enabled and outside buyback_deadtime_seconds before expiration); otherwise it returns 'sell_rejected' and the position settles at expiration. rollover_position moves a losing open position to the next expiration window for a commission (only where the backend has rollover configured; the position must not currently be in the money).

Money safety: each balance has a type — 'regular' is a real-money account, 'training' is a demo account with imaginary funds. There is no default account: place_trade, sell_position and rollover_position act on the balance the position/amount belongs to. Check the balance's type from list_balances before placing — do not assume it. Before any write on a 'regular' balance, confirm the exact order (asset, direction, amount, expiration, balance) with the user and proceed only on explicit approval; prefer a 'training' balance to experiment.

Provenance: never invent ids or numbers — every value you pass to a write tool must come from a prior read in this session (balance_id from list_balances; asset_id, profit_percent and the expiration from list_assets; position_id from list_positions). If a write fails with a not-found error, re-run the matching read tool to refresh the ids before retrying.

Access: there are two distinct reasons a write can be unavailable. (1) Your token lacks the binary-options:write scope — write tools are hidden and calls return a scope/permission error; call get_capabilities, which reports mode 'read-write', 'read-only', or 'none'. (2) Your account is regulatory-blocked from opening positions — list_assets, place_trade and rollover_position return 'trading_access_denied' even with a valid write scope, while sell_position stays allowed so you can wind down open exposure. Do not retry a 'trading_access_denied' error.

Retries & idempotency: every write tool is idempotency-protected. The gateway fingerprints a write by (your user, the tool name, and the exact arguments) for one hour; replaying a byte-identical write inside that hour is rejected with 'idempotency_conflict' instead of placing a second trade. Do not blindly retry a write whose result you did not see — first call the matching read tool to check whether it already took effect. To place a genuinely new trade, change at least one argument. Only successful writes are fingerprinted, so retrying after a validation_error is allowed.

Errors: each error carries a stable 'code' and a 'retryable' flag — only retry when retryable is true ('internal_error', 'rate_limited', 'throttled' after a short backoff). 'validation_error', scope/permission errors, 'trading_access_denied', 'idempotency_conflict', 'insufficient_funds', 'asset_not_available', 'trade_rejected', 'sell_rejected', 'rollover_unavailable' and 'rollover_rejected' are terminal — fix the request or read before re-writing rather than retrying. A 'validation_error' mentioning profit_percent means the payout changed — re-run list_assets and use its fresh profit_percent.

Rate limits: calls are rate-limited per user (shared across the user's tokens) over a rolling window — a global gateway cap counted against every call, plus separate read and write budgets (each tool counts against exactly one; get_capabilities and get_limits count against 'read'). The write budget is the tightest, so batch your reads up front and reserve write calls for trades you actually intend to place. Call get_limits for exact numbers; on a 'rate_limited' error back off using its retry_after_ms / reset_at rather than retrying immediately.

tools.description: Return recent OHLC price candles for an asset (by asset_id from list_assets) so you can gauge the recent trend before opening a position. Required: asset_id and size (candle width in seconds — one of the supported values). Optional count (default 100, max 1000). Each candle has from/to timestamps and open/close/min/max prices.

asset_id.description: Asset id to fetch candles for, from list_assets. Must be positive.

size.description: Candle width in seconds. Must be exactly one of: 1,5,10,15,30,60,120,300,600,900,1800,3600,7200,14400,28800,43200,86400,604800,2592000 (e.g. 60 = 1-minute, 3600 = hourly, 86400 = daily). Any other value is rejected with a validation_error.

count.description: Number of most-recent candles to return. Omit or pass 0 for the default of 100; max 1000. Values above 1000 (or negative) are rejected with a validation_error.

tools.name: get_candles

from.description: The time when the candle begins

to.description: The time when the candle ends

open.description: The price at the start of the candle

close.description: The price at the end of the candle

min.description: The lowest price during that candle

max.description: The highest price during that candle

tools.title: Get candles

tools.description: Report this token's access mode for binary-options: read-write (write tools available to this token), read-only (market data and portfolio only), or none. The mode reflects token scopes; per-account trading restrictions may still apply at call time. Call this to learn why write tools may be absent from the tool list.
tools.name: get_capabilities

product.description: Identifier of the product this MCP server fronts (also the scope namespace used by get_limits and capability checks)

mode.description: Access mode of the calling token for this product: read-write, read-only, or none

tools.title: Get binary-options capabilities

tools.description: Report the gateway's rate limits so you can pace calls and avoid rate_limited errors. Limits are enforced per user — shared across all of that user's tokens, not per token — over a rolling window. There is a global gateway cap across every call, plus separate read and write buckets; each tool counts against one bucket (write tools against 'write', everything else against 'read'). This reports the static limits, not live remaining counts; a rate_limited error already carries retry_after_ms and reset_at.
tools.name: get_limits

product.description: Identifier of the product this MCP server fronts (also the scope namespace)

scope.description: What the limits are keyed on. Always 'per-user': shared across all of the user's tokens

bucket.description: Bucket name: gateway (caps every call), read (read tools), or write (write tools)

limit.description: Maximum requests allowed in one window

window_seconds.description: Length of the rolling window in seconds

buckets.description: Rate-limit budgets. Every call counts against 'gateway'; each tool additionally counts against its 'read' or 'write' bucket

tools.description: Maps each tool name to the read/write bucket it counts against

tools.title: Get binary-options rate limits

tools.description: List your already-closed positions, with paging. Optional skip (records to skip; default 0) and limit (default 50, max 500). Each row has position_id, asset_id/asset_name, direction, amount, open_price/open_time, close_price/close_time, close_reason, the net profit (can be negative), and a result enum: 'win' (expired in profit), 'loss' (expired at a loss), 'equal' (expired flat), or 'canceled' (closed before expiry, e.g. sold early). Page by increasing skip in steps of limit until fewer than limit rows return.

skip.description: Number of records to skip from the start, for paging; default 0, must be >= 0 (negative is a validation_error). To page, set skip = page_index * limit.

limit.description: Maximum records to return. Omit or pass 0 for the default of 50; max 500. A larger or negative value is rejected with a validation_error. Fewer than limit rows means you have reached the end.

tools.name: get_trade_history

position_id.description: Position identifier of the closed position

amount.description: Amount invested, in the balance currency

open_price.description: Quote at which the position was opened

close_price.description: Quote at which the position closed

profit.description: Net profit/loss of the closed position in the balance currency (close proceeds minus the invested amount); negative for a losing trade

close_reason.description: Raw backend reason the position closed: 'win' / 'loose' / 'equal' on a normal expiry settlement, 'sold' when closed early, or a cancellation/rollover state. Use the normalized result field for outcome logic

result.description: Outcome enum: 'win' (expired in profit), 'loss' (expired at a loss), 'equal' (expired flat), or 'canceled' (closed before expiry, e.g. sold early)

tools.title: Get binary-options trading history

tools.description: List tradable assets. Each row has asset_id (pass to place_trade), name, is_open (currently tradable), minimum_amount/maximum_amount for the trade amount, profit_percent (payout percent of a winning trade — pass this exact value to place_trade), the available expirations, and the early-sell (buyback) settings. By default only currently-open assets are returned; set only_enabled=false to include closed ones. Note: if your account is under regulatory trading restrictions this returns a trading_access_denied error — portfolio tools may still work, but new positions cannot be opened.

only_enabled.description: When true (the default), only assets that are currently tradable (is_open=true) are returned; set false to include closed/suspended assets too.

tools.name: list_assets

minimum_amount.description: Default smallest allowed place_trade amount (in the balance currency); an asset that omits minimum_amount uses this value

maximum_amount.description: Default largest allowed place_trade amount (in the balance currency); an asset that omits maximum_amount uses this value

deadtime_seconds.description: Default seconds before an expiration when opening new positions is no longer allowed; an asset that omits deadtime_seconds uses this value

buyback_enabled.description: Default early-sell availability; an asset that omits buyback_enabled uses this value

buyback_deadtime_seconds.description: Default seconds before expiration when early sale stops being available; an asset that omits buyback_deadtime_seconds uses this value

asset_id.description: Asset identifier; pass as asset_id to place_trade

is_open.description: True when the asset is currently tradable (enabled, not suspended, within its trading schedule)

precision.description: Number of decimal places used for this asset's prices

profit_percent.description: Payout percent of a winning trade. Pass this exact value as profit_percent to place_trade; a stale value is rejected. Absent when the backend has no payout configured for this asset

expirations.description: Upcoming expiration times as unix seconds (UTC), already aligned to the asset's start_time and period and past its deadtime. Pass one of these values as place_trade's expired — do NOT compute your own boundary

expiration_sizes_seconds.description: Available position durations in seconds; each is a valid expiration length for opening a new position on this asset

minimum_amount.description: Override of defaults.minimum_amount; if omitted, use defaults.minimum_amount

maximum_amount.description: Override of defaults.maximum_amount; if omitted, use defaults.maximum_amount

deadtime_seconds.description: Override of defaults.deadtime_seconds; if omitted, use defaults.deadtime_seconds

buyback_enabled.description: Override of defaults.buyback_enabled; if omitted, use defaults.buyback_enabled

buyback_deadtime_seconds.description: Override of defaults.buyback_deadtime_seconds; if omitted, use defaults.buyback_deadtime_seconds

tools.title: List binary-options assets

tools.description: List your trading balances. Each row has balance_id, a type ('regular' = real-money account, 'training' = demo account with imaginary funds), currency, available amount, and bonus_amount. Pass the chosen balance_id to place_trade — there is no default balance. Optional types filter: ALL (default), NORMAL (regular only), TRAINING (demo only).

types.description: Optional balance-type filter (case-insensitive). ALL (default; regular + training), NORMAL (regular only), TRAINING (demo only). Omit for ALL; any other value is rejected with a validation_error.

tools.name: list_balances

balance_id.description: The ID of the balance, use this number when placing a trade

type.description: Can be either 'regular' or 'training', where 'regular' means your real account with actual money, and 'training' is your training account with some imaginary funds

currency.description: ISO currency code of this balance; the unit for amount, bonus_amount, and the place_trade amount when trading on this balance

amount.description: Available funds in this balance, in the balance currency

bonus_amount.description: Bonus funds included in this balance, in the balance currency

tools.title: List binary-options balances

tools.description: List your currently open positions on one balance (balance_id from list_balances). Each row carries position_id (pass to sell_position or rollover_position), asset_id/asset_name, direction, amount staked, open_price/open_time, the live current_price, expected_profit (net of the staked amount, negative when losing), sell_profit (net result if sold now), expiration, and seconds_remaining.

balance_id.description: The balance to list open positions for, from list_balances.

tools.name: list_positions

position_id.description: Position identifier; pass as position_id to sell_position or rollover_position

amount.description: Amount invested in this position, in the balance currency

open_price.description: Quote at which the position was opened

current_price.description: Latest quote of the underlying asset

expected_profit.description: Projected net result at expiration in the balance currency (payout minus the invested amount); negative for a currently-losing position

sell_profit.description: Net result in the balance currency if the position is sold now via sell_position (sale proceeds minus the invested amount); negative for a losing position. Omitted when this product does not support early sale, so its absence means the position cannot be sold before expiration

seconds_remaining.description: Seconds left until the position expires

tools.title: List binary-options positions

tools.description: Open a new binary-options position. Pass balance_id (from list_balances), asset_id plus its current profit_percent (both from list_assets), direction 'call' (price will be above the open quote at expiration) or 'put' (below), the amount to stake, and expired — the expiration time as unix seconds (UTC), picked from the asset's expirations list returned by list_assets (do not compute your own boundary — the listed values already respect the asset's period, start alignment and deadtime). Returns the new position_id; review it with list_positions. If the chosen balance is type 'regular' this stakes real money — confirm the trade with the user first; use a 'training' balance to practice. Requires the write scope (see get_capabilities); accounts under regulatory restrictions are blocked with trading_access_denied even with the scope.

balance_id.description: One of the balance_id values from list_balances. The trade is staked against this balance; a 'regular' balance is real money. There is no default — this must be supplied.

asset_id.description: One of the asset_id values from list_assets.

direction.description: 'call' = the price will be above the open quote at expiration, 'put' = below. Any other value is rejected with a validation_error.

amount.description: Amount to stake, in the chosen balance's currency. Must be within the asset's minimum_amount/maximum_amount from list_assets and strictly greater than 0.

profit_percent.description: The asset's current profit_percent exactly as returned by list_assets. A stale or wrong value is rejected with a validation_error — re-run list_assets to refresh it.

expired.description: Expiration time as unix seconds (UTC). Pick one of the values from the asset's expirations list in list_assets — they are already aligned to the asset's start_time/period and past its deadtime. A value not offered there is rejected as misaligned/expired.

tools.name: place_trade

position_id.description: Id of the newly opened position. Pass it to sell_position or rollover_position; list_positions shows its live state.

tools.title: Place trade

tools.description: Move one of your currently open, currently-losing positions to the next expiration window instead of letting it expire, for a commission charged from the balance. Pass position_id and expiration_time — the position's CURRENT expiration as unix seconds; take the position's expiration field from list_positions (an ISO 8601 timestamp) and convert it to unix seconds. The backend derives the next window from it. Returns the resulting position_id. Fails with 'rollover_unavailable' / 'rollover_rejected' when the asset has no rollover configured, the window has closed, or the position is in the money. WRITE action that spends from the balance — confirm with the user on a 'regular' balance. Requires the write scope.

position_id.description: position_id of an open position, from the position_id field of list_positions.

expiration_time.description: The position's CURRENT expiration as unix seconds. Take the expiration field of its list_positions row (an ISO 8601 timestamp) and convert it to unix seconds. The next expiration window is derived from this value; a stale value is rejected.

tools.name: rollover_position

position_id.description: Id of the position after the rollover. Track it with list_positions.

tools.title: Rollover position

tools.description: Close one of your currently open positions early at the current buyback price, before its expiration. Pass a position_id from list_positions (its sell_profit field previews the net result of selling now). Early sale is available only where the asset has buyback_enabled and more than buyback_deadtime_seconds remain before expiration; otherwise the call returns 'sell_rejected' and the position settles at expiration. On success returns a text confirmation. Requires the write scope.

position_id.description: position_id of an open position, from the position_id field of list_positions. History rows (get_trade_history) are already closed and cannot be sold.

tools.name: sell_position
tools.title: Sell position
